name: Reconstruction-Limited Observability Law
purpose: Define observability as bounded reconstruction over accessible continuation topology.

candidate_law_statement.informal: A local observer or reconstruction process can only recover the portion of continuation topology that remains accessible, admissible, and reconstructively distinguishable under finite reachability and compression limits.

formal.observable_subset_candidate: Obs_α(U) := { β ∈ U : β ∈ D_A(α), reconstruction fidelity F_Ξ(α,β) ≥ θ_Ξ, and ambiguity A_Ξ(α,β) ≤ η_Ξ }
formal.reconstruction_fidelity_candidate: F_Ξ(α,β) := F(accessibility_strength, admissibility_margin, compression_loss, perturbation_corruption, orientation_equivalence)
formal.ambiguity_region_candidate: Amb_α := { β : multiple admissible prehistories or continuation structures project to equivalent reconstructed states }
formal.hidden_topology_clause: Stable continuation topology may exist outside Obs_α without being reconstructively accessible to α.
formal.bounded_observability_clause: Observability is local, bounded, reconstruction-limited, and accessibility-conditioned.
formal.non_observer_absolutism_clause: No universal observer, complete reconstruction frame, or global observation standpoint is assumed.
